title: Middle Salesforce Developer
entry: Complete the Junior foundations or demonstrate a small feature with a sound data model, least-privilege access, bulk-safe Apex, meaningful tests, and a basic LWC. CRM and the Northstar actors are restated where needed; unfamiliar product licenses are not assumed.
exit: Build and explain an integrated feature with explicit security, durable operation identity, controlled asynchronous work, failure recovery, usable UI states, and reproducible release evidence.
project: Northstar Motors: Anna and Max manage customer test drives and warranty requests; Oleg supervises work; Irina is a fictional customer. The core project uses custom Vehicle and Test Drive records, then explicitly declared request and diagnostic metadata.

lessons.title: Designing and verifying an access model
lessons.outcome: Turn a business request into separate object, field, record, and operation decisions. Build an access matrix for two sales branches before changing permissions.
lessons.task: Prepare and verify a minimum-permission model for Anna, Max, and Oleg.
lessons.acceptance: Every allowed row identifies its grant. At least three denied operations are tested. No administrator-only evidence is presented as salesperson verification.
lessons.interview: Does object Read grant every record?
lessons.visual: Four nested access gates surrounding one appointment card

lessons.title: Permission Set Groups and muting
lessons.outcome: Predict effective permissions when a permission set group mutes a grant that is also supplied elsewhere.
lessons.task: Submit the four-path experiment with a small diagram and observed results.
lessons.acceptance: The explanation distinguishes group-local muting from effective user permissions. All four assignment combinations are considered. Group recalculation and unchanged record access are recorded.
lessons.interview: Does muting alter the reused permission set?
lessons.visual: Several permission paths converging on one field with a single path blocked

lessons.title: Manual and implicit sharing
lessons.outcome: Identify why a record is visible and distinguish an explicit manual grant from access arising from supported standard relationships.
lessons.task: Produce a short before-and-after report for manual sharing and one supported implicit-sharing relationship.
lessons.acceptance: Each visibility result names an access mechanism. Remaining access after removal is investigated. No claim says all lookups automatically share records.
lessons.interview: Does a manual Read share grant field Read?
lessons.visual: One appointment reached by a manual bridge and a separate relationship bridge

lessons.title: Apex managed sharing across a record lifecycle
lessons.outcome: Maintain a manager's record access while preserving unrelated grants and handling bulk changes.
lessons.task: Implement the transition table on Project__c and submit evidence of safe reconciliation.
lessons.acceptance: No unrelated share is deleted. Cleared and changed managers remove the obsolete owned grant. Bulk and undelete behavior are explicitly tested.
lessons.interview: Why use a custom reason?
lessons.visual: A project card transfers one access key while an unrelated key remains untouched

lessons.title: Restriction rules and supported access paths
lessons.outcome: Filter an already accessible record set for selected users while recognizing object, edition, and execution-context boundaries.
lessons.task: Create the North/South experiment and explain the result for two users.
lessons.acceptance: No new access is attributed to the restriction. Supported object, edition, and context are recorded. Positive, negative, and unaffected-user cases are included.
lessons.interview: Can the rule open a private appointment?
lessons.visual: An already open collection of appointment cards passing through a regional filter

lessons.title: Apex security and API-version defaults
lessons.outcome: Separate class sharing context from database access mode and verify security when changing an Apex API version.
lessons.task: Explain and verify one read path under explicit modes and API-version defaults.
lessons.acceptance: The report separates sharing from CRUD/FLS. API versions are identified. No broad permission is added solely to make the test green.
lessons.interview: Is omitted sharing always without sharing?
lessons.visual: Two versioned execution lanes with separate record and field access gates

lessons.title: Choosing Flow or Apex for a business operation
lessons.outcome: Choose an implementation from the shape of the work, its transaction boundaries, and the team's ability to maintain it.
lessons.task: Choose and implement the confirmation rule, then explain how two larger variants would change your decision.
lessons.acceptance: The choice mentions maintenance and volume. No duplicate automation performs the same responsibility. The failure policy is demonstrated rather than implied.
lessons.interview: Is Flow always preferable for a simple UI?
lessons.visual: One business operation branching toward three simple implementation tools

lessons.title: Order of execution, recursion, and idempotency
lessons.outcome: Explain repeated automation within a transaction and design a durable business result that is not duplicated by re-entry or retries.
lessons.task: Build the declared receipt behavior and demonstrate repeated execution without duplicate results.
lessons.acceptance: Exactly one receipt exists per defined key. Unrelated failures are not called successful retries. The confirmation-cycle limitation is explicit.
lessons.interview: Why does static state not solve a later retry?
lessons.visual: A circular automation path feeding a single durable receipt slot

lessons.title: Structuring Apex and using Custom Metadata
lessons.outcome: Separate warranty business rules, orchestration, and external access without adding layers that have no clear responsibility.
lessons.task: Separate one policy and one business decision from a mixed orchestration sketch.
lessons.acceptance: Dependencies are visible at the entry point. Local tests require no provider or real credentials. Each introduced layer has a stated responsibility.
lessons.interview: Why is request progress ordinary data?
lessons.visual: One large code block separated into policy orchestration and adapter blocks

lessons.title: Testing a complete local business rule
lessons.outcome: Build independent fixtures and meaningful assertions for normal, boundary, invalid, and bulk inputs before introducing network behavior.
lessons.task: Submit a local test suite with boundaries, negative cases, and mixed bulk input.
lessons.acceptance: No business records are read through SeeAllData. Strict cutoff and protected statuses are checked. The mutation fails a relevant assertion.
lessons.interview: Why pass a cutoff instead of reading now everywhere?
lessons.visual: A boundary marker separating one cancelled appointment from three protected appointments

lessons.title: Selecting an asynchronous processing mechanism
lessons.outcome: Match delayed work to its volume, timing, transaction, and recovery requirements without promising immediate execution.
lessons.task: Choose mechanisms for five operations and state the visible result and recovery behavior of each.
lessons.acceptance: Every delayed operation has a pending state or equivalent acknowledgement. Timing is described as a requirement, not an unsupported guarantee. Retry load is included.
lessons.interview: Does enqueue success prove business success?
lessons.visual: Five business tasks sorted into immediate queue batch schedule and event lanes

lessons.title: Queueable Apex and observable request state
lessons.outcome: Create a local background warranty check with a durable request identity, a job reference, and explicit outcomes before adding HTTP.
lessons.task: Implement the local Queueable lifecycle and a bounded manual retry.
lessons.acceptance: One key creates one business request. Job and request IDs are distinguishable. Failed work is visible and retries are bounded.
lessons.interview: Why pass a request ID?
lessons.visual: One warranty request card linked to two distinct background job attempts

lessons.title: Batch Apex and independent execution scopes
lessons.outcome: Process a larger appointment dataset in bounded transactions and report partial failure without implying whole-job atomicity.
lessons.task: Build the cancellation Batch with visible success, skipped, and failed outcomes.
lessons.acceptance: Protected statuses remain unchanged. An error is visible and tied to its record or scope. A repeat run does not corrupt already processed records.
lessons.interview: What persists with Stateful?
lessons.visual: Three processing trays with independent success and failure markers

lessons.title: Scheduling, workload limits, and monitoring
lessons.outcome: Run periodic work with a deliberate overlap policy, time-zone definition, and observable completion.
lessons.task: Add a schedule and a documented monitoring and recovery procedure to M13.
lessons.acceptance: Time-zone assumptions are explicit. Overlap and abandoned-run behavior are defined. The report distinguishes scheduling, execution, and business completion.
lessons.interview: Why can a nightly job overlap?
lessons.visual: A night schedule with one active processing window and a blocked overlapping run

lessons.title: API contracts and credential boundaries
lessons.outcome: Describe the warranty provider's request, response, errors, and identity before connecting a client.
lessons.task: Create a contract and credential responsibility map that another developer can implement without guessing.
lessons.acceptance: Business negative and transport failures differ. Identity and principal permission mapping are explicit. No secret appears in code or documentation.
lessons.interview: What does the Named Credential contribute?
lessons.visual: A request passing through a separate identity key and endpoint gate

lessons.title: Working with REST and SOAP service contracts
lessons.outcome: Read an existing provider interface, select the appropriate client and mock, and preserve its error and authentication semantics.
lessons.task: Write a contract map and demonstrate the appropriate mock for one concrete client.
lessons.acceptance: The selected mock matches the call mechanism. Example XML is not described as a complete WSDL. Live authentication remains an explicitly separate check.
lessons.interview: Must a modern integration use REST?
lessons.visual: Two request envelopes one structured JSON and one nested XML meeting a common result

lessons.title: HTTP callouts, failures, and bounded retries
lessons.outcome: Implement a small warranty client and test success, invalid responses, business absence, throttling, server failure, and transport errors locally.
lessons.task: Implement the mock and bounded orchestration mapping around the supplied client.
lessons.acceptance: All tests run without a provider. A valid negative answer differs from failure. Retry exhaustion is visible and does not loop indefinitely.
lessons.interview: Is covered=false an error?
lessons.visual: One HTTP response split into distinct success missing throttled and invalid outcomes

lessons.title: Inbound APIs, external IDs, and duplicate protection
lessons.outcome: Accept repeated incoming data without creating duplicate business requests, while distinguishing record identity from operation identity.
lessons.task: Build and verify a stable inbound request contract with conflict handling.
lessons.acceptance: One request exists for three identical deliveries. A successful request is not silently restarted. Conflicting key reuse returns an explicit error.
lessons.interview: What does upsert guarantee conceptually?
lessons.visual: Three repeated request envelopes entering one unique business-record slot

lessons.title: Integration diagnostics and controlled recovery
lessons.outcome: Trace a warranty request across attempts and give an operator enough evidence to retry safely without exposing secrets.
lessons.task: Demonstrate how one request can be found, diagnosed, and safely retried.
lessons.acceptance: History survives later success. One correlation key connects request and attempts. Retry authorization and eligibility are explicit.
lessons.interview: Why retain failed attempts after success?
lessons.visual: One request timeline with preserved failed and successful attempt markers

lessons.title: Choosing SOQL or SOSL for a search requirement
lessons.outcome: Use structured queries for known filters and indexed search for words across object types, while handling delayed search visibility.
lessons.task: Create the appointment list and customer search with distinct contracts.
lessons.acceptance: Date boundaries and null lookups are handled. Multiple object types are distinguishable. The indexing limitation is explained without fabricated timing.
lessons.interview: Why use SOQL for tomorrow's appointments?
lessons.visual: A precise calendar filter beside a magnifying glass spanning three record types

lessons.title: Lightning Web Component lifecycle
lessons.outcome: Observe creation, attachment, rendering, removal, and child-error handling without assuming a component renders only once.
lessons.task: Produce a parent-child trace and correct one deliberately introduced duplicate-resource or render-loop defect.
lessons.acceptance: Hook order is observed rather than invented. Repeated rendering is expected. No duplicated external listener remains after reopening.
lessons.interview: Does renderedCallback run only once?
lessons.visual: A component instance moving through creation attachment repeated rendering and removal

lessons.title: Wire, imperative Apex, and refreshing data
lessons.outcome: Separate reactive reads from explicit writes and refresh the cache that actually supplies the displayed data.
lessons.task: Implement a reactive read and explicit confirmation with separate save and refresh outcomes.
lessons.acceptance: The correct refresh API matches each data source. A successful save is not reported as a failed save. Rapid input changes do not display the wrong record.
lessons.interview: What must be passed to refreshApex?
lessons.visual: A saved appointment beside three distinct cache paths with one selected refresh arrow

lessons.title: DOM events and Lightning Message Service
lessons.outcome: Choose a communication contract for related components and for independent regions of the same Lightning application.
lessons.task: Demonstrate DOM events for one component tree and LMS for a separate panel.
lessons.acceptance: Payloads contain only needed identifiers. DOM and LMS responsibilities are distinct. Scope and cleanup behavior are explained.
lessons.interview: When is a DOM event simpler?
lessons.visual: A small upward component event beside a bridge between two independent page panels

lessons.title: Accessible LWC states and Jest tests
lessons.outcome: Test what a user can understand and operate, including keyboard interaction, empty results, failed loading, and selection events.
lessons.task: Build the four UI states and verify selection and recovery behavior.
lessons.acceptance: Tests pass independently with cleanup. Event payload and error recovery are asserted. Keyboard access and readable labels are demonstrated.
lessons.interview: Why flush asynchronous updates?
lessons.visual: An appointment selector with a visible keyboard focus path through four UI states

lessons.title: Shadow DOM and component boundaries
lessons.outcome: Keep DOM, styling, and event contracts inside their intended boundaries and understand the implications for optional legacy migration.
lessons.task: Show owned queries, scoped styles, and a stable public event contract.
lessons.acceptance: No private child DOM is accessed by the parent. The event detail carries the required business identity. Optional Aura work is labeled separately.
lessons.interview: Why can a global selector fail?
lessons.visual: Two component boxes with protected interiors connected by one public event port

lessons.title: Platform Events and publication timing
lessons.outcome: Publish a business fact with a deliberate relationship to commit, and verify the subscriber independently from the publisher.
lessons.task: Create a minimal event path with explicit commit behavior and a duplicate-safe receipt.
lessons.acceptance: Payload contains no unnecessary customer data. Publication timing is stated and checked. The receipt remains unique across repeated delivery.
lessons.interview: Why prefer After Commit for this fact?
lessons.visual: A committed appointment followed by separate publication delivery and receipt milestones

lessons.title: Change Data Capture, replay, and duplicate delivery
lessons.outcome: Choose a record-change stream or business event and recover from disconnection without treating replay IDs as permanent business identities.
lessons.task: Analyze the supplied trace and design both short-disconnection and retention-gap recovery.
lessons.acceptance: The duplicate produces one effect. Replay tokens are treated as opaque. Beyond-retention recovery is defined.
lessons.interview: What does CDC communicate?
lessons.visual: An interrupted event stream reconnecting with one repeated message safely ignored

lessons.title: Git fetch, integration, and cherry-picking a fix
lessons.outcome: Explain the state changed by common Git operations and transfer one focused correction without losing unrelated work.
lessons.task: Create the controlled branch experiment and explain each state transition.
lessons.acceptance: Working tree, index, branch, and remote-tracking state are distinguished. The selected commit is identified from real history. The final content is coherent and unrelated changes are preserved.
lessons.interview: Does fetch update your current files?
lessons.visual: A focused commit moving between two small branch histories

lessons.title: Pull requests, CI checks, and controlled deployment
lessons.outcome: Prepare a reviewable change with truthful validation, metadata dependencies, explicit target environment, and recovery steps.
lessons.task: Create a focused PR and release checklist for one completed Middle feature.
lessons.acceptance: No check is marked passed without evidence. Target org and permissions are explicit. Recovery includes data and external effects where relevant.
lessons.interview: What does a local Jest pass prove?
lessons.visual: A focused change passing through review validation deployment and user verification gates

lessons.title: Verifying an application under failure
lessons.outcome: Test the complete path from user action through background work and mocked provider response to the final visible result.
lessons.task: Verify the integrated feature with controlled failures and one repaired defect.
lessons.acceptance: Duplicate and denied-access cases are included. UI messages match persisted outcomes. No unexecuted check is reported as successful.
lessons.interview: Why can isolated tests all pass while the feature fails?
lessons.visual: A complete request path tested by several controlled failure switches

lessons.title: Enhanced Omni-Channel routing
lessons.outcome: Explain how queued service work becomes eligible for a person based on presence, capacity, and routing configuration, with a complete no-license simulation path.
lessons.task: Submit the provided simulation with three condition changes and an optional separately labeled live observation.
lessons.acceptance: Every chosen or excluded person has a reason. No unsupported tie-breaking rule is invented. Simulation and live evidence are clearly separated.
lessons.interview: Why is a queue not enough?
lessons.visual: One queued case passing presence capacity and skill gates toward a single eligible worker

lessons.title: Agentforce tasks, actions, and evidence
lessons.outcome: Build a clear mental model of an employee agent and verify one bounded read-only action before considering actions that change CRM data.
lessons.task: Complete the ten-case matrix for the read-only contract and optionally demonstrate the live action.
lessons.acceptance: No artificial slot is described as real calendar availability. Unknown and denied inputs are handled explicitly. Simulation and live results are distinguished.
lessons.interview: What does an action add beyond instructions?
lessons.visual: A conversational request connected to one read-only action and a verified result card

lessons.title: Automotive Cloud data modeling
lessons.outcome: Compare the small custom vehicle model with Automotive Cloud's industry entities and decide what additional business requirements would justify the product.
lessons.task: Map the Northstar customer-and-vehicle lifecycle and defend whether additional industry capabilities are needed.
lessons.acceptance: Vehicle__c is not confused with the industry Vehicle API. Relationships are not invented from labels. No unavailable trial blocks the core course.
lessons.interview: Why separate a Vehicle Definition?
lessons.visual: One vehicle model definition linked to individual cars and their changing participant relationships

lessons.title: Middle project review and technical defense
lessons.outcome: Demonstrate a coherent Northstar feature, defend its design with evidence, and repair one unfamiliar failure without relying on optional product licenses.
lessons.task: Deliver the integrated project and complete a short review plus one repair exercise.
lessons.acceptance: Access, duplicate handling, failure recovery, and bulk behavior are supported by evidence. The release plan declares dependencies and actual checks. Required clinic analyses are complete without mandatory live product licenses.
lessons.interview: Which risks should be handed to the next developer?
lessons.visual: A completed service feature surrounded by clear evidence cards and one repaired fault
